clue.text: "Fair game" a toss of the head suggests?

parts.note: coconut is slang for a person's head
to shy is to throw, so a shy is a toss

explanation.surface: Someone tossing their head as if to say a person is fair game for teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts, hence a game at a fair; the quotation marks flag that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The stall is literally a game played at a fair, where throwing wins prizes.

clue.text: Trade ship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a skilled occupation or handicraft
second meaning: a vessel or boat

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words look like an instruction to ship goods; they are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a skilled occupation and a vessel, as in small craft on the water.

clue.text: Sell clue, love, as anagram of carbohydrate

indicators.note: the clue openly says the preceding words are to be rearranged into the result

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, a round O

explanation.surface: A setter telling you to market a clue, nicely, as an anagram of a carbohydrate.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes its own mechanism: sell, clue and love's O rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose is the polysaccharide that makes up plant cell walls, a classic carbohydrate.

clue.text: The lifeboat-men surrounded by wild throngs of merry dancers

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Royal National Lifeboat Institution, Britain's lifeboat charity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lifeboat crews in the middle of crowds of revellers dancing at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrounded by' suggests an insertion, but all the letters are simply mixed together. Merry dancers is an old Scots name for the aurora.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and Shetland the shimmering aurora borealis is traditionally called the merry dancers.

clue.text: Metal wrapper can be frustrating

parts.note: a tin is a can of food
to foil a plan is to frustrate it

explanation.surface: Struggling to open a metal wrapper can be a frustrating business.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin sheet metal used for wrapping food is a literal metal wrapper.

clue.text: Pope's great queen, note, uplifted by a shout of praise

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting something up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: soh, the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale
Alexander Pope's 'great Anna' in The Rape of the Lock is Queen Anne

explanation.surface: A queen celebrated in a poem is raised up by a cheer of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope addresses Queen Anne as 'great Anna' in The Rape of the Lock; the reversed note sits above her name in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a cry of adoration and praise to God, used in Christian worship.

clue.text: Tale of hero going, one…, hundred past the record

indicators.note: past means coming after, so the following items are placed later in the answer

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
Roman numeral one
Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hero's story rolling on, past a hundred, setting a record.
explanation.walkthrough: One and a hundred are Roman numerals placed after the record, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem recounting the deeds of a heroic figure.

clue.text: Hickory about to be planted in the enclosure

indicators.note: planting puts something inside the ground, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A hickory tree is to be planted in a fenced-off field.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a species of hickory tree, so the genus serves as definition by example.

clue.text: Study offer made by the challenger

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a tender is a formal offer

explanation.surface: A study proposal put forward by a rival bidder.
explanation.definitionFit: A challenger for a title is a contender, someone competing to win it.

clue.text: Coward's court-room drama? Not really

parts.note: surface reading: a legal play by Noel Coward
setter's reading: Coward's famous 1945 film, whose title puns on a lawyer's brief and a meeting

explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward wrote the film Brief Encounter; a brief is a barrister's case papers, so the title sounds like a court-room meeting, which the film is not.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1945 David Lean film was written by Noel Coward from his own one-act play, so it is Coward's drama.

clue.text: Banking agent going by air

parts.note: surface reading: someone working for a bank, travelling by plane
setter's reading: the hinged flap on an aircraft wing that makes it tilt in a turn

explanation.walkthrough: Banking is the tilt of an aircraft as it turns, not finance; the agent of that tilt is the movable surface on the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailerons are wing flaps that roll an aeroplane, causing it to bank into a turn in flight.

clue.text: Old Muslim enters a track event between Poles

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within another
between places a piece in the gap separating two others

parts.note: the South and North poles, S and N
taken as written
a race is an athletics track event

explanation.surface: A historical Muslim athlete steps onto the track for a race between Polish rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like people from Poland, but it means the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European name for Arab or Muslim peoples, notably during the Crusades.

clue.text: Try to make a landing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a score in rugby, made by grounding the ball
second meaning: what an aircraft does as it reaches the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Try reads as a verb, attempt, but it is the rugby score; the second half is the verb for an aircraft arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a try is scored by grounding the ball, and planes reach the runway at the same word.

clue.text: Important, namely, as a picker of winners?

definitions.text: Important, namely, as a picker of winners?

parts.note: setter's reading: important is earnest, as in Wilde's play, and by name that is Ernest, whose pet form is the answer
surface reading: a shrewd tipster; setter's reading: the British machine that draws Premium Bond prizes

explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a British government lottery-style savings scheme whose winning numbers are picked by a machine called ERNIE; Ernie is short for the name Ernest, which sounds like earnest, important.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment selects the monthly Premium Bond prize winners.

clue.text: Could be, we hear, the annual output of mill

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, not a spelling

parts.note: an annual is a plant, such as a bloom, that lives one year

explanation.surface: A miller's yearly production could be estimated from rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: Annual looks like an adjective meaning yearly; it is the noun for a plant that lives a single season.
explanation.definitionFit: A flour mill grinds grain into powder, which is its product.

clue.text: This, adjusted, helps a fit between rails

definitions.text: This, adjusted, helps a fit between rails

indicators.note: adjusting something rearranges it, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: This part, properly adjusted, ensures rails fit together snugly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, with 'This' pointing to it, while the last words also supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishplate is a metal bar bolted across a joint to join two railway rail ends.

clue.text: In such property repair holes, putting in lead

indicators.note: repairing something remakes it, so the letters are put together anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plumber fixes holes in a building's pipework using lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead looks like plumbing metal to fill holes; it is just more letters to mix in.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasehold is a form of property tenure held for a fixed term under a lease.

clue.text: Prevalent method of acquisition

definitions.note: an adjective; the answer is the participle of obtain in its sense 'be in force'
definitions.meaning: first meaning: in force or current, as in 'the conditions now ...'
second meaning: the act of getting hold of something

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about a popular way of acquiring things; it is two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain can mean to be established or prevail, as well as to gain or acquire.

clue.text: Polonius' bond of friend ship for musicians

parts.note: setter's reading: Polonius tells Laertes to grapple friends with 'hoops of steel', a metal bond
surface reading: a group of Caribbean players on pans made from oil drums

explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, Polonius advises binding true friends 'with hoops of steel', so his bond of friendship is a band of that metal; the printed 'friend ship' is friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel band is a Caribbean ensemble of musicians playing tuned pans made from oil drums.

clue.text: Sidney's work in the Peloponnese

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sir Philip Sidney's Elizabethan prose romance

definitions.note: the answer is a region within the Peloponnese
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a mountainous region in the southern Greek peninsula

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a book set in Greece; it is two meanings, the romance's title and the Greek region.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney's pastoral romance takes its title from the Greek region idealised as a rustic paradise.

clue.text: Destroyer of neatness?

parts.note: surface reading: something that ruins tidiness
setter's reading: neat means undiluted, as a spirit served without water

explanation.walkthrough: Neatness looks like tidiness, but a neat drink is one taken straight; anything that waters it down ends that state.
explanation.definitionFit: A diluent is a thinning agent, such as water or a mixer added to a straight spirit.

clue.text: Provide pussy with a capital sight

parts.note: pussy is a pet name for a cat
the remaining letters; how these words yield them is not clear

explanation.surface: Feeding your cat a real treat, a sight to make it purr.
explanation.walkthrough: Pussy supplies the first three letters and Provide is the definition; how 'with a capital sight' gives the last two is unclear, perhaps a misprint in the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food or whatever else is needed for an occasion.

clue.text: Patrol-leader called after a crash

indicators.note: after puts one piece behind the other in the answer
the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: the opening letter of the word patrol
rang as in telephoned

explanation.surface: The leader of a patrol phoned in after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: A prang is British slang, originally RAF, for a crash or minor collision.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is informal British slang for a vehicle or aircraft collision, a crash.

clue.text: Mural decoration by painter in classic art

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: ars is the Latin, classical, word for art
RA, Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A wall decoration done by a painter in the classical style.
explanation.walkthrough: Classic hints at Latin, the classical language, and RA is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a rich tapestry hung on a wall, taking its name from the French weaving town.

clue.text: Change of court's oil painter

indicators.note: a change alters the arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal court switches its official oil painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Oil painter reads as one phrase, but oil belongs to the letters and painter alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourist is an artist notable for skilful use of colour, so a type of painter.

clue.text: River city with a council

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a major river of the English Midlands
second meaning: the Italian city, Trento, that hosted a famous Church council

explanation.walkthrough: City with a council sounds like any town hall; it is the Council of Trent, the 16th-century Catholic council held in Trento.
explanation.definitionFit: England's Trent is a long river, and Trent is the old English name for Trento of the Counter-Reformation council.

clue.text: Russell the poet regarded as sparkling

parts.note: AE was the pen name of the Irish poet George William Russell
rated means esteemed or regarded

explanation.surface: A poet named Russell was considered witty and brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: George Russell signed his poems AE, a much-used crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerated drinks are charged with gas, so they are fizzy or sparkling.

clue.text: Implicate ten, fuddled with drink

indicators.note: fuddled means confused by drink, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Ten people, befuddled by alcohol, are dragged into a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Implicate here keeps its root sense, from Latin plicare, to fold or twist together.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate in its older sense is to twist or wreathe things together, as in entwining.

clue.text: The way of world revolution

parts.note: surface reading: a global political uprising, perhaps by communists
setter's reading: the direction in which the Earth spins on its axis

explanation.walkthrough: World revolution suggests politics, where the East had its own associations in 1981; it is the planet turning, which it does towards the sunrise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth rotates from west towards the sunrise, so that compass direction is its way of turning.

clue.text: Maker of vehicles — or the power-loom

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a craftsman who builds carts

definitions.note: stands for the inventor of the power-loom
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Edmund, the English clergyman who invented that machine in 1785

explanation.walkthrough: 'Maker of' carries over to the second half: the maker of the power-loom was the Reverend Edmund Cartwright.
explanation.definitionFit: A wright is a builder, so a cart-builder bears the trade name, also the surname of the loom's inventor.
